messages.content: My wife cannot get away in time for either of the Friday flights we discussed. We can manage the last flight Friday night, or leave early Saturday. Please compare those two, including the hotel difference, and make sure either one gets us there before Saturday dinner.
I’ll recheck the two-person airfare and pair each schedule with the university-area hotel. Is the Monday return still the 4:35 p.m. flight, and is Saturday dinner in Edina still at 6:30 p.m.?
Yes. The graduation is unchanged too. We need to be at dinner no later than 6:30, and I do not want to make the family wait on us.

Both schedules work. The late-Friday option departs Atlanta at 9:35 p.m. and reaches Minneapolis at 11:12 p.m. The Monday return departs at 4:35 p.m. and arrives in Atlanta at 8:02 p.m. Two Main Cabin tickets are $1,058. Graduate by Hilton Minneapolis is $654 total for Friday through Monday, making the flight-and-hotel subtotal $1,712. With about $120 for rideshares, the estimated trip total is $1,832.

The early-Saturday option departs Atlanta at 7:05 a.m. and arrives in Minneapolis at 8:43 a.m. It uses the same Monday return. Two Main Cabin tickets are $984. The same hotel is $438 total for Saturday through Monday, so airfare and lodging come to $1,422. Estimated rideshares are $112, for an estimated trip total of $1,534. You would have nearly ten hours between landing and dinner.
So Saturday saves $298 overall. What is the practical downside besides getting up early?

The main risk is losing the arrival buffer if the outbound is substantially delayed or canceled. On the current schedule, you could tolerate several hours of delay and still reach Edina before dinner. The hotel may not have the room ready when you arrive, but it will store your bags. Friday gives you a full night of protection against same-day disruption, while Saturday avoids one hotel night and has the lower airfare.
What time would we need to leave the hotel for dinner on the Saturday plan? And does arriving Saturday cause any issue with Sunday's ceremony?

I would request a rideshare at 5:40 p.m. Saturday, allowing roughly 25 minutes for the trip plus extra traffic time. Sunday is unaffected: the hotel is still about a 12-minute walk from the ceremony, so leaving at 1:15 p.m. remains appropriate.
All right. Take the Saturday flight and the university hotel for two nights. Before you charge anything, confirm the cancellation terms and the exact amount due now.

The two airline tickets total $984 and are nonrefundable, but their value can be retained as airline credit if canceled under the fare rules; changes may require a fare difference. The hotel total is $438 including taxes and mandatory fees, with free cancellation through 11:59 p.m. local time on May 14. The full airfare and hotel total due now is $1,422. Rideshares are not prepaid.
Does the room still accommodate both of us, and are there any separate resort or destination fees at check-in?

Yes. It is one room for two adults. The quoted $438 includes the mandatory hotel charges shown at booking, and no separate resort or destination fee is listed. Incidental charges would still require a card at check-in.
Good. Book the flights for both of us and that one room. No insurance or other extras.

The trip is confirmed. Delta confirmation V6K2RP covers two Main Cabin passengers from Atlanta to Minneapolis on Saturday, May 16, departing at 7:05 a.m. and arriving at 8:43 a.m., with the return Monday, May 18, departing at 4:35 p.m. and arriving in Atlanta at 8:02 p.m. Airfare charged was $984. Graduate by Hilton Minneapolis confirmation GHM-730518 is for one room for two adults, May 16-18, at $438 total. Hotel cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. Minneapolis time on May 14. The combined amount charged is $1,422. No insurance or optional extras were added. With estimated rideshares, the expected trip total is $1,534.
